title: Plate tectonics
examples: What are the major plates on Earth?
How do plates move relative to each other?
What causes earthquakes at plate boundaries?

explain.say: Today we will learn about the giant plates that make up Earth's surface. These plates are constantly moving very slowly.
When plates move apart, we call this a divergent boundary. Magma rises up to create new crust there. The Mid-Atlantic Ridge is a good example.
When plates move together, this is a convergent boundary. This collision can cause powerful earthquakes and mountains. The Andes Mountains show this process well.
When plates slide past each other, we call this a transform boundary. Crust is neither created nor destroyed here. The San Andreas Fault in California is a famous example.
The collision of continental plates often builds very tall mountain ranges. This process is called orogeny. The Himalayas are a massive example of this.
In everyday life, the movement of tectonic plates affects where we build our cities. We must be careful near active fault lines. This is why building codes are important.

faq.q: Do all plate boundaries cause volcanoes?
faq.a: Not all boundaries cause volcanoes, but many do. Convergent boundaries, especially where oceanic crust meets continental crust, are very active.
asks: Are volcanoes always at plate edges?

faq.q: Are the plates moving fast enough to notice?
faq.a: No, the movement is extremely slow, only a few centimetres per year. This is about the rate your fingernails grow.
asks: How fast do the plates move?
Is the movement noticeable to us?

faq.q: What is the difference between continental and oceanic crust?
faq.a: Continental crust is thicker and mostly made of granite rock. Oceanic crust is thinner and is mainly made of basalt rock.
asks: What rock makes up the ocean floor?
Are the two types of crust different?

faq.q: Why do mountains form at convergent boundaries?
faq.a: Mountains form because the immense compressional force pushes the crust upwards and folds the rock layers. This process is called folding.
asks: How does plate collision make mountains?

faq.q: Are transform boundaries always associated with earthquakes?
faq.a: Yes, transform boundaries are characterized by plates grinding past each other. This friction builds up huge amounts of stress, releasing energy as earthquakes.
asks: Do plates sliding past each other shake things?
What kind of boundary causes shaking?

facts: The Earth's lithosphere is broken into several large tectonic plates.
Divergent boundaries involve the creation of new crust material.
Convergent boundaries can result in subduction or mountain building.
Transform boundaries involve plates sliding horizontally past one another.

quiz.say: If two plates are pulling away from each other, what type of boundary is it?
quiz.why: Divergent boundaries are defined by plates moving away from each other, causing magma to rise.

wrong.0: This is wrong because convergent boundaries involve plates colliding, which is a different type of movement.
wrong.1: This is wrong because all plate boundaries involve significant movement or stress.
wrong.3: This is wrong because transform boundaries involve plates sliding past each other, not pulling apart.

quiz.say: What geological feature is most likely to form at a convergent boundary?
quiz.why: The immense force of colliding plates folds and uplifts the crust, creating mountain ranges.

wrong.0: This feature forms where plates are pulling apart, not colliding.
wrong.1: A fault line is typically associated with plates sliding past each other.
wrong.2: A rift valley forms where crust is pulling apart, not where it is compressed.

quiz.say: If you observe a fault line where movement is purely side-to-side, what boundary type are you seeing?
quiz.why: Transform boundaries are characterized by plates grinding past each other horizontally.

wrong.0: Subduction is a process within a convergent boundary, not the boundary type itself.
wrong.2: This is wrong because divergent boundaries show plates separating from each other.
wrong.3: This is wrong because convergent boundaries involve plates crashing into each other.
